doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Writing 'Dodger Blue'
summary: Asked if he was commissioned by a baseball team, he explains the Dodgers asked him to write the song, recorded with Alan Broadbent and Sue Raney.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I want to ask you about a few of your tunes if you don’t mind. To your knowledge are you the only songwriter who has been commissioned by a baseball team?
I have no idea. And it certainly wasn’t in the form of a commission, it was more of a permission.

Yeah. I mean they asked me if I wouldn’t mind writing it. I mean they kind of invited me to write it. And it’s “Dodger Blue” you’re speaking of. Yeah. But there was no commission involved really. That’s too nice a word for it. It was really, they were nice

enough to ask me to write it and they said that if I did write it they’d be happy to play it over the loudspeaker. So we recorded it with a big orchestra arranged and conducted by Alan Broadbent and Sue Rainey was the singer. And it was indeed used on the public address and other uses.
